headline: PCG Says PLA Fired Flares Toward Unarmed Philippine Aircraft Over Kalayaan Island Group
seoTitle: PLA Fired Flares Toward PCG Aircraft Over Kalayaan | FMB News
seoDescription: The Philippine Coast Guard says PLA forces fired multiple flares toward an unarmed PCG aircraft during a September 7 patrol over the Kalayaan Island Group.
deck: The Philippine Coast Guard says Chinese forces discharged multiple flares toward an unarmed PCG aircraft during a September 7 maritime patrol near Zamora and Panganiban Reefs.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Philippine Coast Guard said forces of China's People's Liberation Army discharged multiple flares toward an unarmed PCG aircraft conducting a maritime domain awareness flight over the Kalayaan Island Group on September 7, 2026.

According to the PCG, Chinese forces at Zamora Reef, also known as Subi Reef, challenged the aircraft over radio before firing flares in its direction. The PCG said Chinese forces at Panganiban Reef, also known as Mischief Reef, later did the same.

The Coast Guard did not report that the Philippine aircraft was hit. GMA News reported that it sought comment from the Chinese Embassy in Manila and had not received a response as of its September 10 report.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The PCG said its aircraft was conducting a routine maritime domain awareness mission and was preparing to land on Pag-asa Island. The aircrew also reported seeing a considerable number of Chinese maritime militia vessels inside the lagoons of Zamora and Panganiban Reefs.
PCG Commandant Admiral Ronnie Gil Gavan said firing flares at an aircraft in flight endangers flight safety and cited China's duty of due regard under the Convention on International Civil Aviation.

The incident is separate from the September 2 encounter over Bajo de Masinloc in which the Armed Forces of the Philippines said a Chinese J-10 intercepted a Philippine government patrol aircraft. The two events occurred on different dates, in different areas and involved different Philippine aircraft.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: The incident concerns the safety of Philippine government personnel conducting patrols in the West Philippine Sea and the country's ability to document maritime activity around features it considers part of its lawful maritime entitlements.

Panganiban Reef is a low-tide elevation within the Philippines' exclusive economic zone and continental shelf under the 2016 South China Sea arbitral award. Beijing rejects the ruling. Repeated close or hazardous encounters also increase the risk of miscalculation even when no collision or injury occurs.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for any formal response from Beijing, a diplomatic protest or other action from Manila, and whether the PCG releases additional flight data, imagery or operational details from the September 7 mission.

FMB News will also monitor whether similar flare incidents recur during Philippine air patrols around the Kalayaan Island Group and whether either side changes operating procedures following the encounter.

The PCG reported no strike on the aircraft. Beijing had not publicly responded to GMA News as of its report. Read the verified facts and context on FMB News.
verificationNotes: The central event is based on the Philippine Coast Guard statement republished by the Philippine Information Agency and independently reported by PNA, GMA News, ABS-CBN News and The Philippine STAR.
FMB News does not characterize the flares as weapons fire beyond the PCG's confirmed description and does not claim the aircraft was hit.
GMA News reported that the Chinese Embassy in Manila had not responded to its request for comment as of publication; FMB News does not infer Beijing's position from silence.

The September 7 Kalayaan incident was checked against FMB's archive and is treated as a separate event from the September 2 Bajo de Masinloc J-10 interception because the date, location, aircraft and conduct differ.
The hero and social images are FMB-owned editorial graphics using the approved purple-violet/plum identity. They do not fabricate or simulate documentary photography.
